title: Classification / Odd One Out — In-Depth Guide — Part 6 of 16

questions.question: What does 'Gender Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words/terms share a common grammatical or biological gender category, with one breaking it
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group shares a common gender category (masculine, feminine, or neutral terms), identifying the one that doesn't fit.

questions.question: What does 'Male/Female Classification' test, specifically?
options: Whether a group of terms are all male (or all female) versions of a role/species, with one being the opposite gender term
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of terms are all consistently male or all female versions (like Lion, Tiger, Bull all being male animal terms), identifying the outlier.

questions.question: What does 'Singular/Plural Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of words are all consistently singular (or all plural), with one breaking that consistency
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of words are all in the same grammatical number (all singular or all plural), identifying the one that breaks that consistency.

questions.question: What does 'Living/Non-Living Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of items are all living (or all non-living), with one item belonging to the opposite category
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of items are all consistently living or all non-living, identifying the item that belongs to the opposite category.

questions.question: What does 'Natural/Man-Made Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of items are all naturally occurring (or all man-made), with one item breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of items are consistently natural or consistently man-made, identifying the item from the opposite category.

questions.question: What does 'Solid/Liquid/Gas Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of substances share the same state of matter, with one being in a different state
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of substances share the same physical state of matter (solid, liquid, or gas), identifying the one in a different state.

questions.question: What does 'Conductors Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of materials are all electrical conductors (or all insulators), with one breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of materials share the same electrical conductivity property (all conductors or all insulators), identifying the exception.

questions.question: What does 'Planet Classification' test?
options: Whether a group of planets share a common categorical property (e.g., all rocky, or all gas giants), with one breaking that pattern
questions.rationale: This tests whether a group of planets share a common astronomical category (like being rocky planets or gas giants), identifying the exception.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Mathematical Property Matrix' introduced around this point in the lesson?
options: To eliminate the need for any property checks
To organize and compare multiple numeric properties (prime, square, etc.) across a set of numbers systematically
A matrix with no practical use
questions.rationale: This matrix systematically organizes multiple candidate numeric properties across a set of numbers, making it easier to spot which shared property connects most of them.

questions.question: What does a 'Classification Decision Tree' provide?
options: A step-by-step branching path for narrowing down which type of classification rule applies to a given group
A synonym for the mathematical property matrix
questions.rationale: A decision tree provides a systematic, branching path to help narrow down which classification rule type applies to a given problem.
